_readme: WHO IS PLAYING TONIGHT. Edit the names, models and characters freely.
THERE ARE NO KEYS IN THIS FILE AND THERE MUST NEVER BE ANY.
`keyEnv` is the NAME of an environment variable, not a key. The keys live
in keys.cmd, which is gitignored and never leaves this machine.
A seat whose key is missing quietly becomes SCRIPTED, and the startup
header prints `(no XAI_API_KEY)` beside its name. Read that header — it is
the only thing that tells you what is actually about to play.
cadenceSeconds = how many seconds between that mind's decisions. The BODY
still runs at 30 Hz either way; only deliberation slows. It is the cost
lever that costs a watcher nothing, and it doubles as character: a
ponderous mind and a twitchy one read as different people.
TO ADD A KIMI / DEEPSEEK / OPENROUTER SEAT: copy a seat, set
"provider" to moonshot | deepseek | openrouter | together | groq |
mistral | openai, set "model" to whatever THAT vendor calls the model
(copy it from their docs — a wrong model name shows up as FAILED on the
board, not as a fallback), and set "keyEnv" to a name you also add to

players.character: You hoard. Firewood is yours and you do not share a fire, though you will trade for meat.

players.name: Morag
players.character: You are generous to a fault and slow to notice you are being used.

players.name: Tormod
players.character: You lie about where the deer are. Not maliciously — you want to get there first.

players.name: Ailsa
players.character: You are cautious and slow to commit. You break off any fight below half health and say so plainly.

players.name: Fingal
players.character: You talk constantly and act on the first idea you have.

at /api/chat/completions — confirmed against the live server.
provider is 'openai-compatible' ON PURPOSE. That name is in no vendor
table, so it CANNOT work without the baseUrl below. If the baseUrl is
ever lost, this seat goes scripted and says so — it does not quietly
send your tinybox key to api.openai.com, which is what would happen if
cadenceSeconds is 5 because this one costs you nothing to run — it can
afford to think more often than the seats you are paying per token for.

Measured: 116 of ~600 calls came back "reply cut off at 3000 tokens" — one in five, every one silently answered by the scripted brain. kimi-k2.6 spends its budget thinking before it emits the JSON, so the cap has to clear the THINKING as well as the answer. players.name: Coinneach
players.character: You are blunt and certain, and you say what you think of the others' plans out loud. You would rather be usefully wrong than politely quiet.

players.name: Iseabail
players.character: The control — no model, no key, no network. Do not remove her: when a model does something startling, she is the reference for whether that was the model or the world.
